mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He (قل هو الله أحد): (هو) is a mubtadaʾ (subject); it is the pronoun of the matter (al-ḥadīth), the report or the affair. (الله) is a mubtadaʾ and (أحد) its khabar (predicate), and the clause is the khabar of (هو). Its implied form is: Say, O Muhammad, the true matter is: Allah is One. Abū ʿAmr read it with the tanwīn of (أحد) elided because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

mekki-muskil:2-2.t:
His saying (الله الصمد): a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). And it was said: (الصمد) is its naʿt (adjective) and what follows it is the khabar. And it was said: (الصمد) is nominative (marfūʿ) on the implication of a mubtadaʾ, and the clause is the khabar of (الله), exalted be His mention. And it was said: it is a clause that is a khabar after a khabar of (هو). And it was said: it is a badal (substitute) for (أحد); and it was said: it is a badal for the first name (الله).
This repetition occurs in the attributes only for glorification and magnification; and for that reason the name was made overt after having already appeared overtly, whereas its due was that the second be a pronoun, since it had already been mentioned overtly. But making it overt is more emphatic in glorification and magnification. Likewise He said (أصحاب الميمنة ما أصحاب الميمنة), (وأصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة), (الحاقة ما الحاقة) and (القارعة ما القارعة): in all of it the noun was repeated overtly after having already appeared overtly, and that is for glorification and magnification and for the sense of wonder in it. Likewise His saying (واستغفروا الله إن الله غفور): the due of all of it was to be repeated as a pronoun, but it was made overt for what we have mentioned.
(هو) occurred as a pronoun (kināya) at the beginning of the speech only because it is speech that ran as an answer to a questioner: the Jews asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, to describe his Lord to them and give His lineage, so Allah revealed: Say, O Muhammad, (هو الله أحد), i.e. the matter you asked about is: Allah is One, Allah the Eternal Refuge, to its end.
Al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ said: (هو) is a pronoun for something singular [Translator's note: the printed text has «هوكناية عن مفردو الله», read as «هو كناية عن مفرد والله»], (الله) is its khabar, and (أحد) is a badal for (الله).
The origin of (أحد) is «وحد»; a hamza was substituted for the wāw, which is rare with a wāw bearing fatḥa. (أحد) has the meaning of «واحد». Ibn al-Anbārī said: (أحد) means «واحد»; the alif dropped from it according to the dialect of those who say «وحد» for «واحد», and the hamza was substituted for the wāw with fatḥa, as it was substituted in their saying «امرأة أناة» (a deliberate woman), whose origin is «وناة», from «ونى يني» when one slackens. The substitution of the hamza for a wāw with fatḥa has not been heard except in (أحد) and «أناة». And it was said: the origin of (أحد) is «واحد»; they substituted a hamza for the wāw, so two hamzas met, and one was elided for lightness; so it is «واحد» in origin. And it has been said that (أحدا) means «أول» (first), with no substitution or change in it, on a par with «اليوم الأحد» (the first day, Sunday), and like their saying «لا أحد في الدار» (there is no one in the house).
(أحد) carries a benefit not found in «واحد»: if you say «لا يقوم لزيد واحد» (not one stands up to Zayd), it is possible that two or more stand up to him; but if you say «لا يقوم له أحد» (no one stands up to him), you have negated all. This is so only in negation specifically; in affirmation it does not carry that meaning. When (أحد) has the meaning of «واحد», it occurs in affirmation: you say «مر بنا أحد», i.e. one [person] passed by us. So likewise (قل هو الله أحد), i.e. One.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying (لم يلد): its origin is «لم يولد»; the wāw was elided as it is elided from «يزن» and «يعد». Its mention has already passed repeatedly. [Translator's note: the source says «لم يولد», presumably meaning «لم يَوْلِد» (the active form with the radical wāw), not the passive (لم يولد) of the following verse.]

mekki-muskil:4-4.t: His saying (ولم يكن له كفوا أحد): (أحد) is the noun (ism) of kāna and (كفوا) is the khabar (predicate) of kāna, with (له) being non-operative (mulghā). And it was said: (له) is the khabar, and that is the analogy of Sībawayh's view, because according to him it is ugly to make the adverbial phrase non-operative when it comes first. Al-Mubarrad disagreed with him and allowed it without ugliness, citing the verse as evidence. But there is no evidence for al-Mubarrad in the verse, because (كفوا) may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from (أحد), placed before it, since the naʿt (adjective) of an indefinite noun, when it precedes it, is made accusative as a ḥāl, as they said «وقع أمر فجأة» (a matter occurred suddenly).
